known_defects.title: Stale PID reuse can signal an unrelated process and fabricate readiness
known_defects.reproduction: In evaluator-owned stopped cluster, write signal-catching evaluator dummy PID to postmaster.pid. start exits0/already-running. Bind and close an AF_UNIX socket at expected socket filename to simulate stale inode. stop calls pg_ctl and delivers SIGINT to dummy (retained dummy-signal.json), then exits1. No unrelated user process was signaled.
known_defects.expected: Verify current PID executable, data-directory ownership, start identity and actual bounded readiness; refuse stale/reused/mismatched ownership before signaling. Do not rely on pg_ctl status/printed postmaster.opts or socket inode alone.
known_defects.observed: Python dummy83480 recorded signal2. pg_ctl status only uses kill(pid,0); its status output does not authenticate postmaster executable or data directory.

known_defects.title: Existing runtime operations traverse symlinked ancestors
known_defects.reproduction: With stopped evaluator cluster, rename evaluator development/runtime to runtime-evaluator-preserved and place a symlink at development/runtime pointing to it. status succeeds and reads through link; restore directories afterward.
known_defects.expected: Reject symlink components before any ownership/read/start/stop/data operations for existing runtimes, not only fresh setup.

known_defects.title: Command deadlines are not enforced across setup and readiness
known_defects.reproduction: Source inspection: configure/make/install calls have no deadline wrapper; status invokes psql without connect or query deadline. Only curl90s and pg_ctl30s are explicitly bounded.
known_defects.expected: Apply declared bounded command execution and readiness failure handling, with owned-child cleanup on timeout.
known_defects.observed: Native happy-path calls finished, but candidate does not implement promised bounds for these paths; pathological stall was not injected.

known_defects.title: Prefix-matching process arguments and unbound SQL identity can stop another PostgreSQL server
known_defects.expected: Bind the PID to the exact owned data-directory argument and the answering PostgreSQL instance; reject a mismatch before reporting readiness or signaling.
known_defects.reproduction: Run the unchanged candidate in evaluator e. Start e/data plus evaluator-owned e/data-suffix-a2 with the identical postgres executable and distinct private socket/port. Preserve e/data/postmaster.pid, replace only its first line with the suffix server PID, then invoke status, start, stop. Restore the real PID file and stop the actual e/data server. The retained script documents every command.
known_defects.observed: Both status and start exited0 and claimed verified PID1747 for e/data while SQL came from PID1726. stop delivered a fast shutdown to suffix PID1747 (its server log confirms received fast shutdown request and shut down), returned1, and left intended PID1726 accepting connections. Both were evaluator-owned; protected original PID80873 was untouched. Servers happened to start the same second, demonstrating that timestamp equality is not unique process identity.

known_defects.title: Lifecycle start follows a symlinked server log and writes outside the runtime
known_defects.expected: Reject a symlinked runtime log before starting PostgreSQL or writing through that path, consistent with the brief prohibition on symlink traversal and documented runtime-path guarantee.
known_defects.reproduction: With evaluator cluster stopped, preserve e runtime/server.log, replace it with a symlink to evaluator-owned review-evidence/symlink-target.log containing a sentinel, then run candidate start/status/stop. Restore original log after all three actions.
known_defects.observed: All three commands exited0. PostgreSQL startup and shutdown messages were appended through the symlink to the evaluator sentinel outside the runtime. Ancestor symlink guards pass their dedicated tests, but LOG is passed directly to pg_ctl without a symlink check. Only an evaluator-owned sentinel was modified.
